text:
Owen Tippett is a 28-goal scorer playing like a man whose name keeps showing up in trade columns. Last season he scored 28 goals and 51 points; this season he has two goals in 16 games, and the rumors have followed (NHLTradeRumor.com linked him to Seattle on Nov. 8). His ice time has slid with it: 15.1 minutes a night overall, under 12 in two of his last three games.

The chances have dried up more than the luck has turned. His individual expected goals per 60 is 0.73, down from 1.22 last season, and the Flyers get only 38% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. He's shooting 5.7% against a usual rate near 12%, so a few more will go in, but our range puts him at 13 to 26 goals for the season, not 28.

The tools haven't gone anywhere: 98th-percentile top speed, a 93 mph shot, and, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, 60% of his shots off the rush last season. He even dropped the gloves in Columbus on Friday. What we'd watch is minutes. A rush winger on 11 a night doesn't get many rushes.
